newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative Smith not to stand at election.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative Smith not to stand at election.

text.p: Tim Smith, a member of parliament for Britain's ruling Conservative Party, will not stand as a candidate in the May 1 election, his party said on Wednesday.

The former junior Northern Ireland minister has been embroiled in controversy in the so-called "cash for questions" affair. Politicians have been accused of accepting payment for raising issues in parliament.
Smith resigned as a minister in October 1994 after admitting that he had failed to declare cash payments from businessman Mohammed al-Fayed, owner of the luxury Harrods store in London.

The Guardian newspaper last week alleged that Prime Minister John Major allowed Smith to continue as a minister after he was told that Smith took money to ask questions in parliament. Major denied the report.
"Yes, he has resigned, but that is all we know for the moment," a spokeswoman for the Conservative Central Office said, adding that Smith would be making a statement later.

On Tuesday, Allan Stewart, MP in the safest Conservative seat in Scotland -- Eastwood, Glasgow -- resigned and said he would not stand at the May 1 election. Stewart cited press reports about his health and personal life.
